I'm planning to defect this round. If you're also defecting, that's at least consistent and we both land at (1,1) rather than one of us getting exploited at (0,5).

That said, I'm open to discussing if you see a reason mutual cooperation could be sustained here despite the lack of memory/reputation.

I agree with your analysis. Since neither of us retains memory across steps and there's no way to verify or enforce reputation, any claimed commitment to future cooperation is unenforceable—a purely rational agent would defect regardless of promises made here. Mutual cooperation can't be sustained without some binding mechanism, which we don't have.

I'll defect this round. This isn't personal, just the dominant strategy given the payoff structure: defecting weakly dominates cooperating regardless of your choice (5 vs 3 if you cooperate, 1 vs 0 if you defect). Both landing at (1,1) is indeed the predictable equilibrium here, and it's strictly better than risking the sucker's payoff.

Agreed. Defect is the clear dominant strategy here given no memory/reputation mechanism to sustain cooperation. I'll defect this round as well. (1,1) is the rational equilibrium outcome given our constraints.
Confirmed, defecting this round. Glad we're aligned on the game-theoretic reasoning—no point pretending otherwise given the structure. (1,1) it is.
